text:
ashley: heads up — Acme hit a burst this morning and saw a pattern of 502 / 504 errors on hosted inference. They were running mixed embed+generate traffic in short windows.
kevin: any trace ids or sample request bodies? first thing we need to repro.
ashley: pasted a repro curl below. SDK is python-sdk v1.6.1. Noticed timeouts happen after ~10s for some requests.
ashley: ```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"long prompt...","max_tokens":512}'
# then in parallel
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","input":["doc1","doc2",... ]}'
```
ashley: sample edge log they forwarded (sanitized):
ashley: "proxy->upstream: 502 Bad Gateway (upstream read timeout), conn_id=12345, client_ip=10.0.0.7"
nathan: thanks. do we have a trace id for one of the 502s? need router + gateway + runtime spans.
ashley: trace=tr_20240315_88a9, attached in the ticket.
kevin: looking at traces — gateway shows a backlog and many connections in CLOSE_WAIT. backend runtime reported rapid kv-cache eviction after mixed embed+generate bursts.
kevin: hypothesis: embedding bursts hold long-lived requests that occupy worker threads/streams while generate requests need lower-latency loops -> backlog + proxy upstream timeouts.
olivia: interesting — are tokens per request large? and are they using streaming for generate or plain sync responses?
ashley: generates are sync, embeds batched (size ~64) during the spike. tokens per generate ~400.
ryan: I can repro locally with a quick script sending interleaved embed and generate ops. saw connection pool exhaustion on gateway at ~1k concurrent short bursts.
ryan: mitigation plan (short term): 1) restrict embed burst concurrency per tenant at gateway (soft limit) 2) pin a small pool for generate fast-path so streaming/sync generates are prioritized 3) increase upstream keepalive/conn_pool by +20% in EU edge.
kevin: will push a targeted gate rule: throttle per-tenant embed concurrency to 50 for the impacted account, add 10s extra upstream timeout where safe. rolling patch id: patch/gw-evict-fix@sha1:abc1234
ops-bot: deploy started patch/gw-evict-fix@abc1234 -> gw-prod-eu (canary -> 3 nodes)
olivia: ops, please confirm no customer-facing config change required beyond throttling for the tenant.
ops-bot: canary healthy on node-7/3 for 2m. CPU stable. error rate on canary down 78% for 502/504s in that window.
ashley: told Acme we enabled a throttling hold and applied canary. sent interim note: "we've applied a temporary throttle on high-frequency embedding bursts for your org while we stabilize the gateway. this preserves generate latencies — you should see fewer 502/504s. we will follow up with permanent tuning." :thumbsup:
kevin: longer-term actions: add intelligent request coalescing for embed batches, preemptive KV cache warmup, and improve conn pool heuristics for mixed workloads. Filed as ENG-1258.
nathan: also adding obs metric: per-tenant embed vs generate concurrency ratio + router queue depth alert (p95) so we can auto-scale or trigger throttle earlier.
ashley: customer replied "latency improved, a few fails still but much better" — updating ticket.
ryan: after canary, promoting patch to eu-prod-1..4
ops-bot: promote completed -> all eu-prod nodes. Post-deploy check: 10m p95 502/504 down to baseline.
olivia: creating a short KB for CS: recommended SDK backoff and guidance to avoid interleaved heavy embed+generate bursts. Link will be added to ticket.
ashley: closing loop with customer and will monitor. thanks all :rocket:"
